description: Mixed-precision dense eigensolver to attack the FP64 cuSOLVER floor on the big dense gapless shapes 6/7/11 (n=512/1024): B200 FP64 is ~37 TFLOPS (weak) and syevd's tridiagonalization is memory-bound, so an FP32 syevd moves half the bytes and runs meaningfully faster than the FP64 syevd these shapes currently use. Mechanism: run cusolverDnSsyevd (FP32) for the eigenpairs, then recover FP64 gate accuracy by refinement — FP64 CholeskyQR2/Newton orthonormalization of Q to fix the orth gate, plus a FP64 Rayleigh-Ritz correction (Vt A V re-diagonalize, near-diagonal) and/or Rayleigh-quotient/subspace-iteration steps to sharpen eigenpairs for the eig/recon gates. Targets compute/memory throughput (avoid weak FP64); keep the per-matrix residual gate + FP64 cuSOLVER fallback, route guarded per shape.

PREMISE PROBE (default off, parent routing => geomean unchanged). Verified brief's FP64-syevd premise is FALSE: input is FP32 so torch.linalg.eigh already calls cusolverDnSsyevd (FP32); nsys shape11 confirms sytrd4_cta<float>/laed3<float2,float>. Raw batched-eigh per shape FP32/FP64: sh6 164174/195842us, sh7 105681/133744us, sh11 203202/214823us. Parent custom already beats the FP32 floor 1.53x(sh6)/2.03x(sh11); sh7 parent==FP32 floor (106717). FP32-vs-FP64 gap only 1.06-1.27x, and shapes never pay FP64 -> no FP64-floor headroom to capture.

Rayleigh-Ritz refinement (brief's EIG/RECON mechanism) bolt-on for sign-DC shape11, env-gated off => committed geomean 28606us == parent. Measured shape11 (parent 99842us): Ritz ON NS=18 -> 296064us (+196ms; Ritz's n x n re-diag megakernel costs more than the two K=300 blocks it refines); Ritz ON NS=6 -> 282474us; Ritz OFF NS=6 -> 291092us (fewer NS -> fuzzy sign -> mass cuSOLVER fallback, confirming NS=18 is the tuned sweet spot). Verdict: FP64/3xTF32 Rayleigh-Ritz refinement is MORE expensive than the coarse solve it would cheapen; no crossover on shape 11.

Cheap first-order Rayleigh-Ritz off-diag correction (brief's 'off-diagonal correction suffices'), env-gated off => committed geomean 28600us == parent. Measured shape11 (parent 99842us): cheap Ritz NS=18 -> 315291us (+215ms). Root cause: shape11 gapless near-degenerate spectrum -> first-order denominators L_i-L_j tiny -> corrections masked out (useless) while 3 extra n x n GEMMs add 215ms. The near-degeneracy that makes these shapes hard breaks gap-denominator refinement; sign-function subspace approach (no gap denominators) is the right structure. Profiled shape7 mixed1024=plain cuSOLVER FP32: 70% GEMV/SYMV tridiag-bound (768 symv+2338 gemvx launches, only ~7% laed3) = memory-bound regime, but heterogeneous so batched reduced-precision solvers can't route the whole batch.

Route shape7 (mixed1024, the one headroom shape at FP32 floor 106717us, 70% memory-bound tridiag) through batched sign-DC-large, env-gated off => committed geomean 28592us == parent, 39/39 valid. RESULT: gate CLEARS whole batch (nbad=1/60, orth 1.08e-2 eigr 1.45e-2) but shape7 -> 181228us (1.70x SLOWER than cuSOLVER FP32). The sign-DC's fixed tensor-core GEMM overhead (A^2 power + ~16 NS sign iters x2 n=1024 GEMMs + CQR bases + 2 ~600-wide cluster blocks + NS finish) EXCEEDS per-matrix Ssyevd at n=1024/b=60 -- sign-DC wins homogeneous n=512 b=640 (huge serial cuSOLVER cost) but loses n=1024 b=60 (bigger fewer matrices amortize cuSOLVER, sign-DC overhead dominates).

4 trials, all env-gated off so committed geomean holds at parent 28592us (39/39 valid, 'stream' absent, -O3). PREMISE DISPROVEN by live measurement: input is FP32 so torch.linalg.eigh already calls cusolverDnSsyevd (FP32) -- nsys shape11 confirms sytrd4_cta<float>/laed3<float2,float>, NO Dsyevd anywhere; and raw FP32 Ssyevd PASSES all 39 gates with ZERO refinement (gates are FP32-normwise, so there is no FP64 accuracy to recover -- the brief's whole refinement premise is moot). Raw batched-eigh FP32/FP64 per shape: sh6 164174/195842, sh7 105681/133744, sh11 203202/214823us; parent CUSTOM already beats the FP32 floor 1.53x(sh6)/2.03x(sh11) -- FAR more than the 1.06-1.27x FP32-vs-FP64 gap the shapes never even pay. MECHANISM TESTED 4 ways, all measured slower on the targets: (t2) full Rayleigh-Ritz on sh11 296064us (+196ms, the n x n re-diag megakernel costs more than the two K=300 blocks); (t3) cheap first-order off-diag Ritz 315291us (+215ms; sh11 gapless near-degeneracy -> tiny L_i-L_j denominators -> corrections masked useless while 3 extra GEMMs add cost -- the near-degeneracy that makes these shapes hard BREAKS gap-denominator refinement); (t4) route sh7 through batched sign-DC-large: gate CLEARS whole batch (nbad=1/60) but 181228us = 1.70x SLOWER than cuSOLVER FP32 (sign-DC's fixed GEMM overhead exceeds per-matrix Ssyevd at n=1024/b60; sign-DC only wins the huge-serial n=512 b640 regime). KEY: the brief's reduced-precision-bulk-plus-refinement mechanism is ALREADY REALIZED and tuned in the tree's sign-DC/megakernel/cluster paths (sh11 profile: 42% FP16 mega_eigh_med_split + 15% TF32 gemm + FP32 NS/Rayleigh refine) -- that IS what gives sh11 its 2.03x over FP32 syevd. OPENINGS still worth a brief: (1) sh7 mixed1024 is the one shape at the FP32 floor and is 70% memory-bound cuSOLVER tridiag (768 symv + 2338 gemvx launches for b60) -- NOT sign-DC-shaped (heterogeneous, loses); the untested lever is a BATCHED BF16/FP16 tensor-core blocked-Householder TRIDIAGONALIZATION (replace the thousands of tiny per-matrix GEMV launches with batched GEMMs across the whole b60 batch, then batched stedc), a from-scratch batched dense eigensolver distinct from the sign-function split; (2) sh6 mixed512 is dominated by a low-PR bulk (407/640 at PR<60) that is LOW-RANK-winnable (a low-rank peel brief, not mixed-precision); (3) push the sign-DC's 15% TF32 sign-iteration GEMMs to BF16 (2250 vs 1100 TFLOPS) -- the sign only needs robustness to precision -- for a partial win on sh11 (untested; ~15% of the shape, needs a bf16 _lr_lift_gemm mode). All probe scaffolding (MP_MODE/MP_RITZ/MP_NS_ITERS/MP_SDC7, _mp_ritz_refine, _mp_ritz_cheap) is committed and env-gated off for reuse.
